method_card.title: Holidays and Travel Plans
method_card.content:
Key Vocabulary

SpanishEnglish
las vacacionesthe holidays
ir de vacacionesto go on holiday
viajarto travel
la playathe beach
las montañasthe mountains
el campothe countryside
el extranjeroabroad
el veranothe summer
el año pasadolast year
me gustóI liked it
me encantóI loved it
me lo pasé bienI had a good time
me gustaríaI would like
sería emocionanteit would be exciting

Grammar Focus — Preterite and Conditional

Use the preterite for completed past actions: fui (I went), viajé (I travelled), nadé (I swam). The preterite of ir is irregular: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron. Use the conditional to say what you would do: take the infinitive and add -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían. Irregular stems: tener → tendr-, hacer → har-, poder → podr-.

Model Paragraph

"El verano pasado fui de vacaciones al campo con mi familia. Nadé en el río y monté en bici. Me lo pasé muy bien. El año que viene me gustaría ir a Grecia porque sería emocionante."
(Last summer I went on holiday to the countryside with my family. I swam in the river and rode a bike. I had a great time. Next year I would like to go to Greece because it would be exciting.)
steps: Learn the key holiday vocabulary and time phrases
Master the preterite tense of ir and regular -ar verbs
Practise forming the conditional with -ía endings
Build paragraphs that combine past, present, and conditional tenses

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — holidays appear in every exam series

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'El verano pasado fui de vacaciones a España con mi familia.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Break the sentence into chunks: El verano pasado | fui de vacaciones | a España | con mi familia.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: El verano pasado = last summer. Fui = I went (preterite of ir). De vacaciones = on holiday.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: A España = to Spain. Con mi familia = with my family.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Last summer I went on holiday to Spain with my family.

worked_examples.question: Which verb form is correct? 'El año pasado _____ (ir) a la playa.' — fui, fue, or ir?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Identify the subject: no explicit subject, but the sentence is about yo (I) — first person singular.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Ir in the preterite is irregular: yo fui, él/ella fue. The infinitive ir cannot be used after a time phrase like el año pasado.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: fui — the yo form of ir in the preterite.

worked_examples.question: Translate to Spanish: 'Next year I would like to travel abroad because it would be exciting.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Next year = El año que viene. This signals the conditional tense.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: I would like to travel = me gustaría viajar. Abroad = al extranjero.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Because it would be exciting = porque sería emocionante. Sería is the conditional of ser.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: El año que viene me gustaría viajar al extranjero porque sería emocionante.

bronze.question: Match the Spanish to the English meaning
Match the Spanish to the English meaning
Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: de vacaciones a España y me lo

gaps.correct_explain: fui is the yo form of ir in the preterite tense.

wrong.fue: fue is the él/ella form, not yo. First person preterite of ir = fui.
wrong.ir: ir is the infinitive. You need the preterite because el verano pasado signals a completed past action.

gaps.correct_explain: pasé is the yo form of pasar in the preterite. The phrase is me lo pasé bien (I had a good time).

wrong.paso: paso is the present tense. The time phrase el verano pasado requires the preterite.
wrong.pasó: pasó is the él/ella form. The subject here is yo.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence

gaps.correct_explain: gustaría is the conditional form — me gustaría means 'I would like'.

wrong.gusta: gusta is the present tense (I like). You need the conditional to say 'I would like'.
wrong.gustó: gustó is the preterite (I liked it). The sentence is about a future wish, so use the conditional.

gaps.correct_explain: la playa means 'the beach'.

wrong.montaña: montaña means 'mountain' — a valid place but doesn't match the word bank here.

gaps.correct_explain: An adjective describing why you'd want to go — relajante (relaxing), emocionante (exciting), or divertido (fun) all work.

wrong.relajar: relajar is a verb (to relax). You need an adjective after sería.

bronze.question: What does 'El año pasado fui de vacaciones a Grecia' mean?
options: Last year I went on holiday to Greece
Next year I will go on holiday to Greece
I would like to go on holiday to Greece
I always go on holiday to Greece

bronze.question: What does 'Me gustaría viajar al extranjero porque sería emocionante' mean?
options: I would like to travel abroad because it would be exciting
I like travelling abroad because it is exciting
I travelled abroad because it was exciting
I will travel abroad because it will be exciting

method_card.title: Accommodation and Hotels
method_card.content:
Key Vocabulary

SpanishEnglish
un hotela hotel
un albergue juvenila youth hostel
un campinga campsite
una casa rurala holiday cottage
una habitación individuala single room
una habitación doblea double room
con bañowith a bathroom
con vistas al marwith sea views
la llavethe key
el ascensorthe lift
quisiera reservarI would like to book
¿Cuánto cuesta por noche?How much per night?
no funcionait doesn't work

Grammar Focus — Imperfect for Descriptions

Use the preterite for the action of staying (me alojé — I stayed) and the imperfect for descriptions of what it was like (era grande — it was big, tenía piscina — it had a pool). Use quisiera (I would like) for polite requests in role-plays.

Model Paragraph

"Me alojé en un hotel de lujo cerca de la playa. La habitación era grande y tenía vistas al mar. Me gustó mucho porque era muy cómodo."
(I stayed in a luxury hotel near the beach. The room was big and had sea views. I liked it a lot because it was very comfortable.)
steps: Learn the key accommodation and hotel vocabulary
Master polite booking phrases with quisiera
Practise combining preterite and imperfect for past accommodation
Learn complaint phrases for hotel role-plays

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — hotel role-plays and accommodation descriptions

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Quisiera reservar una habitación doble con baño, por favor.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Quisiera = I would like (polite conditional of querer). Reservar = to book.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Una habitación doble = a double room. Con baño = with a bathroom.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I would like to book a double room with a bathroom, please.

worked_examples.question: Which tense? 'El hotel _____ (ser) bonito y _____ (tener) piscina.' — era/fue and tenía/tuvo?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Both clauses are descriptions of what the hotel was like — not completed actions.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: For descriptions in the past, use the imperfect: era (it was) and tenía (it had).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: El hotel era bonito y tenía piscina. The imperfect is used for past descriptions.

bronze.question: Match the Spanish to the English meaning
Match the Spanish to the English meaning
Complete the sentence

gaps.correct_explain: Quisiera means 'I would like' — the polite form used for booking in role-plays.

wrong.Quiero: Quiero means 'I want' — it's correct but less polite. Quisiera is the expected form in exam role-plays.
wrong.Quería: Quería is the imperfect (I wanted/used to want). Use quisiera for a polite request.

gaps.correct_explain: Doble = double. Individual = single. Both are valid room types.

wrong.grande: grande means 'big' — it's an adjective, not a room type. Use doble or individual.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence

gaps.correct_explain: era is the imperfect of ser. Use it for descriptions of what something was like.

wrong.fue: fue is the preterite of ser. For describing what the hotel was like (ongoing characteristic), use the imperfect era.
wrong.es: es is the present tense. You're describing a past hotel, so use the imperfect.

gaps.correct_explain: tenía is the imperfect of tener. Use it to describe what something had (ongoing feature).

wrong.tuvo: tuvo is the preterite of tener. For describing features of a place (it had a pool), use the imperfect tenía.
wrong.tiene: tiene is the present tense. You're describing a past hotel.

gaps.correct_explain: alojé is the yo preterite form of alojarse (to stay). The action of staying is completed.

wrong.alojaba: alojaba is the imperfect. Since we're stating a single completed stay, use the preterite alojé.
wrong.alojo: alojo is the present tense. You're describing a past hotel stay.

gaps.correct_explain: tenía is the imperfect — describing what the room had (an ongoing feature).

wrong.tuvo: tuvo is the preterite. For describing features, use the imperfect tenía.
wrong.tiene: tiene is present tense. The sentence is about a past stay.

method_card.title: Transport and Directions
method_card.content:
Key Vocabulary

SpanishEnglish
en cocheby car
en trenby train
en aviónby plane
en autobúsby bus
en barcoby boat
en biciby bike
a pieon foot
siga todo rectogo straight on
tuerza a la derechaturn right
tuerza a la izquierdaturn left
cerca denear
enfrente deopposite
al lado denext to

Grammar Focus — Comparatives

Use más ... que (more ... than), menos ... que (less ... than), and tan ... como (as ... as) to compare transport. Key adjectives: rápido (fast), lento (slow), caro (expensive), barato (cheap), cómodo (comfortable). Use mejor que (better than) and peor que (worse than) for irregular comparatives.

Model Paragraph

"Prefiero viajar en tren porque es más rápido que el autobús y más cómodo que el coche. Ir en bici es mejor para el medio ambiente."
(I prefer to travel by train because it is faster than the bus and more comfortable than the car. Going by bike is better for the environment.)
steps: Learn transport vocabulary including en + vehicle and a pie
Master comparatives: más/menos ... que, mejor/peor que
Practise giving and understanding directions
Learn prepositions of place for describing locations

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — transport comparisons and direction role-plays

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'El tren es más rápido que el autobús pero más caro.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: El tren = the train. Es = is. Más rápido que = faster than.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: El autobús = the bus. Pero = but. Más caro = more expensive.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: The train is faster than the bus but more expensive.

worked_examples.question: Which preposition? 'La farmacia está _____ del banco.' (next to the bank)

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: 'Next to' in Spanish is al lado de.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Del is the contraction of de + el (of the, masculine).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: La farmacia está al lado del banco.

bronze.question: Match the Spanish to the English meaning
Match the Spanish to the English meaning
Complete the sentence

gaps.correct_explain: más ... que means 'more ... than'. This is the standard comparative.

wrong.menos: menos ... que means 'less ... than'. The sentence says the train is faster, so use más.
wrong.muy: muy means 'very' — it doesn't compare two things. Use más ... que for comparisons.

gaps.correct_explain: que means 'than' in comparisons. Más rápido que = faster than.

wrong.como: como is used with tan (tan ... como = as ... as), not with más.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence

gaps.correct_explain: al lado de means 'next to'.

wrong.lejos: lejos de means 'far from' — possible but check context.

gaps.correct_explain: enfrente de means 'opposite'. Cerca de means 'near'. Both are valid.

wrong.dentro: dentro de means 'inside' — a station is not inside a park.

bronze.question: What does 'Ir en bici es mejor para el medio ambiente' mean?
options: Going by bike is better for the environment
Going by bike is faster than the bus
I like going by bike because it is fun

bronze.question: What does '¿Cómo se va a la estación de tren?' mean?
options: How do you get to the train station?
Where is the bus stop?

Key Vocabulary

Grammar Focus — Past Continuous

The past continuous describes what was happening: estar in the imperfect + gerund (-ando for -ar verbs, -iendo for -er/-ir verbs). Example: Estaba nadando (I was swimming). Combine with the preterite for scene-setting: Estaba tomando el sol cuando empezó a llover (I was sunbathing when it started to rain).

Model Paragraph

"El verano pasado fui de vacaciones a la playa. Hacía sol y el agua estaba clara. Cada mañana nadábamos en el mar y por la tarde tomábamos el sol. Estaba descansando cuando empezó a llover."
(Last summer I went on holiday to the beach. It was sunny and the water was clear. Every morning we swam in the sea and in the afternoon we sunbathed. I was resting when it started to rain.)
steps: Learn weather expressions using hace, llueve, nieva, hay, and está
Master holiday activity vocabulary in present and past tenses
Practise the past continuous (estaba + -ando/-iendo) for scene-setting
Combine preterite, imperfect, and past continuous in a paragraph

Key Vocabulary

Grammar Focus — Four Tenses

Show range by using four tenses: Present (Uso mi móvil cada día), Preterite (Ayer mandé mensajes), Imperfect (Antes no tenía móvil), Future (En el futuro usaré la tecnología para trabajar). The perfect tense (haber + past participle) adds further range: He comprado un portátil nuevo (I have bought a new laptop).

Model Paragraph

"Uso mi móvil cada día para mandar mensajes y buscar información. Por un lado, es útil porque puedes mantenerte en contacto con amigos. Por otro lado, paso demasiado tiempo en las redes sociales."
(I use my phone every day to send messages and search for information. On one hand, it is useful because you can keep in touch with friends. On the other hand, I spend too much time on social media.)

Master phrases for advantages and disadvantages

Key Vocabulary

Grammar Focus — Hay, Tiene, and Prepositions

Use hay (there is/are) to describe what is in a room: En mi dormitorio hay una cama. Use tiene (has) for what your house has: Mi casa tiene un jardín. Prepositions of place describe position: encima de (on top of), debajo de (under), al lado de (next to). For the past: había (there was/were) and tenía (had). For ideal home: conditional — tendría (would have), habría (there would be).

Model Paragraph

"Mi casa tiene tres dormitorios, un salón grande y un jardín pequeño. En mi dormitorio hay una cama cómoda al lado de la ventana y un escritorio encima del cual hay una lámpara. Mi casa ideal tendría una piscina enorme."
(My house has three bedrooms, a big living room, and a small garden. In my bedroom there is a comfortable bed next to the window and a desk on top of which there is a lamp. My ideal house would have a huge pool.)

Grammar Focus — Se Puede and Opinions

Use se puede + infinitive to say what you can do: Se puede ir de compras (You can go shopping). Negative: No se puede hacer mucho (You can't do much). Use lo mejor es que / lo peor es que for balanced opinions. Conditional for ideal town: Mi ciudad ideal tendría (My ideal city would have), habría (there would be).

Model Paragraph

"Vivo en un pueblo pequeño. Hay un parque, una biblioteca y muchas tiendas. Lo mejor es que es tranquilo. Lo peor es que no hay cine. Mi ciudad ideal tendría un cine y más restaurantes."
(I live in a small village. There is a park, a library, and many shops. The best thing is that it is quiet. The worst thing is that there is no cinema. My ideal city would have a cinema and more restaurants.)

method_card.title: The Environment and Global Issues
method_card.content:
Key Vocabulary

SpanishEnglish
el medio ambientethe environment
la contaminaciónpollution
el cambio climáticoclimate change
el calentamiento globalglobal warming
el reciclajerecycling
la basurarubbish
reciclarto recycle
ahorrar energíato save energy
ahorrar aguato save water
apagar las lucesto turn off the lights
las energías renovablesrenewable energy
proteger el medio ambienteto protect the environment
plantar árbolesto plant trees

Grammar Focus — Obligation and Future

Use se debe + infinitive (one must), deberíamos + infinitive (we should), hay que + infinitive (it is necessary to), and es importante + infinitive (it is important to) for obligations. The future tense is formed by adding endings to the infinitive: -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án. Example: Reciclaré más (I will recycle more). Irregular stems: tener → tendr-, hacer → har-, poder → podr-.

Model Paragraph

"Hago todo lo posible para proteger el medio ambiente. Reciclo, no malgasto agua y voy en bici al instituto. Deberíamos usar menos plástico. En el futuro usaremos energías renovables."
(I do everything possible to protect the environment. I recycle, I don't waste water, and I go to school by bike. We should use less plastic. In the future we will use renewable energy.)
steps: Learn environmental problems and eco-friendly actions vocabulary
Master obligation phrases: se debe, deberíamos, hay que, es importante
Practise the future tense for discussing environmental plans
Use three tenses in a paragraph about the environment

exam_context.frequency: Higher Tier favourite — environment appears in writing and speaking

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Se debe reciclar más para proteger el medio ambiente.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Se debe = one must / you should. Reciclar más = recycle more.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Para = in order to. Proteger el medio ambiente = protect the environment.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: You should recycle more to protect the environment.

worked_examples.question: Form the future tense: 'Nosotros _____ (usar) energías renovables.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Future tense = infinitive + ending. Nosotros ending = -emos.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Usar is regular → usar + emos = usaremos.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Nosotros usaremos energías renovables. (We will use renewable energy.)

gaps.correct_explain: Se debe means 'one must' or 'you should'. It is an impersonal obligation phrase.

wrong.puede: se puede means 'one can' — it's about ability, not obligation.
wrong.quiere: se quiere means 'one wants'. The sentence needs obligation, not desire.

gaps.correct_explain: After para (in order to), use the infinitive: proteger (to protect).

wrong.protege: protege is a conjugated form (he/she protects). After para, use the infinitive proteger.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence

gaps.correct_explain: reciclaré is the yo future tense of reciclar (infinitive + -é).

wrong.reciclo: reciclo is the present tense. En el futuro requires the future tense.
wrong.reciclé: reciclé is the preterite (I recycled). The sentence is about the future.

gaps.correct_explain: malgastaré is the yo future of malgastar (to waste). Gastaré also works.

wrong.malgasto: malgasto is the present tense. The future requires malgastaré.
wrong.malgasté: malgasté is the preterite. This is about the future, not the past.

silver.question: Complete the sentence
silver.english: We **should** use public transport and we **will** plant more trees.

gaps.correct_explain: Deberíamos = We should (conditional of deber, nosotros form).

wrong.Debemos: Debemos means 'We must' (present). 'We should' is softer → conditional deberíamos.
wrong.Podemos: Podemos means 'We can'. The English says 'should', not 'can'.

gaps.correct_explain: plantaremos is the nosotros future of plantar (infinitive + -emos).

wrong.plantamos: plantamos is the present (we plant). The English says 'we will plant' → future.
wrong.plantaríamos: plantaríamos is the conditional (we would plant). The English says 'we will' → future.
